title: The Best Black Friday iPhone Deals
summary: Cellular carriers have always offered big savings on the newest iPhone models during the holidays, and Black Friday 2026 is no different, with major discounts at AT&T and T-Mobile , as well as Best Buy . Right now we're tracking notable offers on the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. For even more savings, keep an eye on older models during the holiday shopping season. Note: MacRumors is an affiliate partner with some of these vendors. When you click a link and make a purchase, we may receive a small payment, which helps us keep the site running. T-Mobile iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max : Up to $1,400 off with eligible T-Mix plan iPhone Duo : Up to $2,100 off with eligible T-Mix plan Apple Watch SE 3: No cost (up to $300) when adding a watch line on a qualifying plan, or get $250 off any Apple Watch when picking up another Apple Watch T-Mobile has quite a few notable offers live for Black Friday , including discounts for the new iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. These offers come under T-Mobile's newly revamped "T-Mix" unlimited plans . With the new T-Mix plans, both the 256GB iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro models are available at no cost, but there is of course a catch. This would require the highest-priced T-Mix plan to get the most "Picks" that you could apply to your new iPhone purchase. UP TO $1,400 OFF iPhone 18 Pro at T-Mobile UP TO $2,100 OFF iPhone Duo at T-Mobile Thankfully, T-Mobile's new structure still allows for other deal options as well. For example, with the iPhone Duo you can still get up to $1,200 off via monthly bill credits by using three of your Picks and trading in an older device, or even up to $830 off via monthly bill credits with one Pick. For the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max , you can up to $1,400 off on an eligible T-Mix plan with five of your Picks. This offer requires qualifying credit, a new voice line, and a $35 device connection charge, after which you'll receive the offer via monthly bill credits. In terms of older model iPhones, T-Mobile is offering four models of the 256GB iPhone 17e at no cost , plus four lines for $25 per line per month. You'll need to add four new lines on the T-Mix Standard plan. AT&T iPhone 18 Pro : No cost with eligible trade-in iPhone 18 Pro Max : Up to $1,200 off with eligible trade-in iPhone Duo : Up to $1,200 off with eligible trade-in Over at AT&T , you can get the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max for up to $1,200 off with an iPhone trade-in in any condition. You'll need to upgrade with AT&T Next Up Anytime or switch to get this offer. UP TO $1,200 OFF iPhone 18 Pro at AT&T UP TO $1,200 OFF iPhone Duo at AT&T Additionally, new and existing customers can get up to $1,200 off the iPhone Duo with an eligible trade-in. If you're switching to AT&T, the carrier will give you up to $800 to pay off your current device balance, and you can save $200 per line when ordering the smartphone online. In regards to the main offer of up to $1,200 off the iPhone Duo, AT&T says this requires an eligible trade-in of $230 or more, alongside activation of a new line or upgrading an existing line. You'll get this credit over the course of 36 months on your AT&T bill. You can find the breakdown of each plan tier from AT&T below, and remember that they each require a trade-in as well. Up to $1,200 off iPhone Duo: requires AT&T Premium 2.0 plan or higher / trade-in value of $230 or more Up to $930 off iPhone Duo: requires AT&T Extra 2.0 plan or higher / trade-in value of $130 or more Up to $500 off iPhone Duo: requires Value 2.0 plan / trade-in value of $130 or more Up to $350 off iPhone Duo: requires any eligible unlimited plan / trade-in value of $35-$129 If you switch to AT&T from a different carrier, AT&T will pay off your phone balance at up to $800 off per line. With the $1,200 offer, AT&T is offering the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro at no cost. Best Buy iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max : Up to $1,200 off with qualified activation and trade-in iPhone Duo : Up to $1,200 off with qualified activation and trade-in Carriers aren't the only place you can save on iPhones this year, with Best Buy offering the same discounts as AT&T and T-Mobile with activation through these carriers at the time of purchase. This is a great option for anyone who shops at Best Buy a lot and likes to rack up member reward points. UP TO $1,200 OFF iPhone 18 Pro at Best Buy UP TO $1,200 OFF iPhone Duo at Best Buy Similar to the carriers, you can get the iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo for up to $1,200 off with qualified activation on cellular plans and a trade-in of an older device. title: GTA VI Now (Barely) Running on Apple Silicon Macs
summary: "Grand Theft Auto VI" can theoretically now run on Apple silicon Macs via unofficial community projects, despite Rockstar Games offering no official Mac version. Developers have adapted the Xbox Series version of the game to work on macOS unofficially, with some reporting that they can explore scenes and control the camera. Unfortunately, the projects remain experimental and performance is too slow for normal play. Mac owners can already play GTA VI through Remote Play from a compatible console. These unofficial projects instead run the game locally on the Mac itself. One project, " Halfwave ," reports around 3 frames per second in a prison scene and almost 5 frames per second during a boat sequence on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 48GB of memory. A separate test with 1080p output reached 6 frames per second in the boat scene. The developer also says saved games and free roam work, although lighting errors, flickering objects, and slow-loading scenery remain. Halfwave builds on " VIctory-macOS ," another community effort to run the game on Apple's chips. A tester using an M2 Pro Mac reported reaching the opening movement tutorial and controlling the camera, but at approximately one frame every two seconds. The projects use several translation tools as a workaround to make the Xbox game work on a Mac. Rosetta 2 handles processor instructions, CrossOver Wine provides Windows compatibility, and Apple's D3DMetal translates graphics into a format the Mac can display. AI tools are also helping with the projects. Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar's parent company, is already targeting efforts to bring the game to other platforms unofficially. A copyright complaint published by GitHub alleged that a similar project called "Leonida" infringed Take-Two's rights. GTA VI launched on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and Series S. Rockstar has not yet announced plans to bring it to the Mac. title: iPhone 18 Production Delay Leaves Apple Little Time Before Launch
summary: Apple's upcoming iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e models are reportedly suffering from another production delay. In a new post on Weibo, the leaker known as "Fixed Focus Digital" claimed that neither model has entered mass production, with the start pushed back from late October to around New Year's Day in 2027. In October, the same source pointed to late November as the production target for the standard ‌iPhone 18‌ and suggested Apple was preparing to build a large inventory. The latest claim cites a different earlier deadline, but January would be later than either of the previously reported targets. Fixed Focus Digital previously suggested that Apple will use some of the same manufacturing processes and components for the two phones. The leaker recently shared a diagram purporting to show identical batteries and 6.3-inch displays for both, although reports disagree about whether the iPhone 18e's screen will increase in size. Expected upgrades include an A20 chip in both models , while other rumors point to 9GB of RAM , up from 8GB, and Apple's C2 modem. Larger batteries have also been rumored, with a potential front-facing camera upgrade for the iPhone 18e. Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman recently identified February or March as the expected introduction window for both devices. If that schedule holds, a January production start would give Apple less time than usual to accumulate stock before launch. title: iPhone 20 Pro Rumored to Feature 3D-Printed Titanium Frame
summary: Next year's iPhone 20 Pro models will make extensive use of 3D-printed titanium in their frames, based on the latest rumor coming out of China. In a new post on Weibo, the leaker known as "Fixed Focus Digital" claims that Apple plans to manufacture parts of the device's mid-frame using a laser-based titanium powder 3D-printing process – one which would result in significantly improved durability. The leaker is apparently so confident in the accuracy of the rumour that they even suggested followers take screenshots of the Weibo post and reference it next year when the device is announced. Earlier this month, Fixed Focus Digital claimed that Apple would return to titanium for next year's 20th-anniversary iPhone models. The iPhone 18 Pro models currently use aluminum frames. Apple already uses the 3D-printing technique to produce the titanium cases of the Apple Watch Ultra 4 and titanium Apple Watch Series 12 models, after the company debuted the process with the Ultra 3 and Series 11. Apple also uses it for the iPhone Air's USB-C port enclosure. The process involves using lasers to fuse successive layers of titanium powder. Apple says this allows for more complex structural designs than conventional manufacturing methods, and significantly reduces material waste. The technology could give Apple greater design flexibility as it develops its rumored all-glass 20th-anniversary iPhone design, which is expected to feature curved glass and virtually invisible display bezels . Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman has described the planned changes as the biggest overhaul of the Pro line since the iPhone X. What remains unclear is how Apple intends to address the thermal challenges associated with titanium, given the superior heat dissipation properties of the aluminum used in its current Pro models. Apple is expected to launch the iPhone 20 Pro series in the fall of 2027. Leakers have referred to the devices as the "iPhone 20 Pro," but Apple's actual naming plans are unknown. title: iPhone Share of US Smartphone Market Hits 57% as Rivals Slip
summary: U.S. smartphone shipments fell 9% year-over-year in the third quarter of 2026, and yet Apple grew its share of the market from 50% to 57%, according to the latest U.S. Market Monitor data from Counterpoint Research . Apple was the only major manufacturer to avoid a shipment decline in the quarter. Counterpoint put the wider market decline down to rising memory costs, which hit Android manufacturers hardest at the low end. Thin margins leave little room for these vendors to absorb higher component prices without raising their prices or cutting volume. Samsung held its ground at 25% share, up one point year-over-year, thanks to its flagship Galaxy S and Z series devices and the low-end Galaxy A-series. But it was Motorola that took the biggest hit – its share fell four points to 8% as memory costs squeezed its large low-end lineup, essentially reversing the share growth it posted in the second quarter. Meanwhile, Google's Pixel 11 launch was not strong enough to prevent a slight decline in share. Smartphone sales at the Big Three carriers already declined 4% year-over-year in Q3, and Counterpoint similarly expects weak Q4 sales as consumers increasingly time purchases around the best deals. Last month, Counterpoint's global third-quarter data likewise showed Apple gaining share in a shrinking smartphone market .
